future_steps.text: Add a runnable example application with a small custom plugin and completion provider, exercising the documented configuration and transport paths end to end.
Add integration coverage for malformed model tool calls, unknown tools, schema-invalid arguments, tool failures, timeouts, and cancellation so the runtime’s failure behavior is explicit.
Define and enforce a stable public API boundary, including compatibility expectations for plugin interfaces, configuration fields, runtime events, and transport adapters.
Add session persistence and resume support so conversations and tool state can survive process restarts rather than remaining memory-scoped.
Introduce bounded resource controls for plugin execution, including concurrency limits, output-size limits, and protection against runaway tool-call loops.
Add release automation that builds the package, validates the published artifact from a clean environment, and checks the README’s installation example against the released interface.

features: Run a model-driven tool-calling loop with custom completion providers
Load plugins that define tools, schemas, and optional prompt sections
Configure the runtime with validated YAML settings
Enable session-scoped time and todo tools
Observe structured runtime events or log them directly
Compact conversations with a sliding window
Reuse the same solver across multiple applications
head_story.text: The README now presents the package as a reusable, capability-agnostic tool-calling runtime for applications that provide their own plugins and product experience. It clearly documents installation, configuration, plugin composition, operational settings, sample usage, supported transports, and current project status.

detail.body:
Refresh the README to present the project as a reusable
LLM tool-calling runtime and make the top-level docs easier
to scan.

The update adds a clearer overview, standardizes section
names and tables, and tightens feature and configuration
descriptions. It also improves the sample layout and status
notes so readers can understand the project scope and setup
more quickly.

+## Overview
+
+Use `llm-platform` when you want a reusable model-driven tool loop without hardcoding domain logic into the host. Define capabilities as plugins, load them per app, and reuse the same runtime across multiple products.
 
 ## Features
 
 - Tool-calling loop with injected `completion_fn` (default: LiteLLM Completions)
-- Plugin host: schemas, callables, optional prompt sections

 - Sliding-window conversation compaction
 - Experimental OpenAI Responses transport (`api.kind: responses`)
